items.title: U.S. inflation rises again and keeps the pressure on Fed
items.content: The main inflation gauge used by the Federal Reserve to set U.S. interest rates rose sharply in August, underscoring why the central bank raised interest rates earlier this month for the first time in three years.

items.title: I’m 71 and still working. I earn $108,000 a year. Am I doing the right thing?
items.content: “I have $152,000 in my IRA and Roth accounts.”

items.title: Meta is pitching a bold new identity — and the payoff could be big
items.content: Enterprise tools present a compelling business opportunity as Facebook and Instagram parent Meta looks to diversify its revenue away from advertising.

items.title: He’s been badmouthing Treasury bonds since 2020, but ‘the big fat cushion’ of 5.25% yields is turning this strategist bullish
items.content: Investors have become accustomed to returns distorted by artificially low interest rates. 5% on bonds and 6% on stocks are more realistic and Bianco finds value in U.S. Treasury notes now.

items.title: ‘I’m afraid of human stupidity’: Why this top economist prefers U.S. tech and gold over bonds
items.content: A prominent economist doesn’t fear artificial intelligence, but fully embraces it in portfolios. He feels far differently about government debt.

items.title: Citi tells investors it’s time to sell Moderna after 600%-plus stock gains
items.content: Revenue and profit forecasts fail to justify the hype baked into Moderna’s share price, according to Citi’s analysts.

items.title: Boeing was at risk of losing all fighter-jet production altogether. Now the stock is up on a new Navy contract.
items.content: Shares in the aerospace company rose close to 3% in premarket trading on Wednesday after the U.S. Navy selected it to develop its next-generation fighter jet.

items.title: Why Tuesday was one of the most disturbing days for markets in recent memory, according to a Goldman Sachs pro
items.content: Beneath the languished moves in the main stock-market indexes, there were some disturbing features.

items.title: One group of funds is holding up the stock market. Barclays says oil prices have to fall to drive a year-end rally.
items.content: Strategists at the bank said a rally at the end of the year would likely depend on oil prices lowering or stabilizing even as the historically best-performing quarter approaches.

items.title: There’s a new Wall Street ‘TACO’ index — and this one is saying it’s time for Trump to strike a deal
items.content: JPMorgan has devised a “TACO” barometer, referring to the expression Trump Always Chickens Out, as a way to predict the behavior of the mercurial world leader.
